title: Proper birational modifications are isomorphisms near codimension one
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, and let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper birational morphism with $Y$ reduced [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Birational means that $f$ maps the generic points of the irreducible components of $Y$ bijectively onto those of $X$ and induces isomorphisms on their local rings [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be the maximal open subset over which $f$ is an isomorphism. Then $U$ contains (1) every codimension-zero point; (2) every codimension-one point $x$ for which $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; (3) every point $x$ with normal local ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] for which the underlying fibre $f^{-1}(\{x\})$ is finite; and (4) every point $x$ with normal local ring such that $f$ is quasi-finite at some $y\in Y$ with $f(y)=x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Codimension of $x$ here is $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover.

source.place: Stacks Project Tag 0BFP (varieties-lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1), all four clauses

proof.text: [lem-sfb-birational-generic-isomorphism-open] gives a dense isomorphism open $V_0$ containing all component generic points. Codimension-zero points are component generic points, so $V_0\subseteq U$ proves (1).

For (4), fix $x,y$ as stated. By [lem-sfb-birational-integral-normal-neighbourhood], choose an integral affine neighbourhood $T$ of $x$ with integral inverse image and restrict $f$ to $T$. Properness persists by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change].

Choose affine source and target neighbourhoods of $y$ and $x$ witnessing [pqf-def-quasifinite]. They can be taken inside the integral neighbourhood of Step 2: take a target principal open containing $x$ inside the intersection and then a source principal open containing $y$ inside its preimage; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-prime-principal-localization] preserves quasi-finiteness. Rename their rings $A,C$ and their primes $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$. The map $A\to C$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], the affine domains $A,C$ embed in their generic local rings. Birationality identifies these with a common field $K$, the fraction field of both $A$ and $C$. The maps into $K$ agree with $f$ by functoriality of germs. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] the two stalks are $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $C_{\mathfrak q}$. Apply [lem-sfb-quasifinite-normal-local-birational-algebra] to obtain that the actual stalk map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (4), affine witnesses and local algebra.

proof.text: Properness gives local finite type and separatedness [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Apply [lem-sfb-invertible-stalk-neighbourhood-section] to the restriction over $T$, obtaining $x\in W\subseteq T$ and a section $W\to f^{-1}(W)$. Both schemes are integral, being nonempty opens of the integral schemes in Step 2. The open $V_0\cap W$ is nonempty: the generic point of $T$ lies in both opens. Thus [lem-sfb-integral-generic-section-isomorphism] applies to this restricted map and section, giving inverse isomorphisms. Hence $x\in U$, proving (4).

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (4), section and closed-section argument.

proof.text: For (3), suppose $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is normal and the fibre over $x$ is finite. The fibre is nonempty: $f(Y)$ is closed by [pqf-lem-proper-basic] and contains the dense isomorphism open of Step 1, hence equals $X$. Choose $y$ above $x$. By [pqf-lem-locqf-fibre-discrete], $f$ is quasi-finite at $y$, since $f$ is locally of finite type and this fibre is finite. Clause (4), proved in Steps 2--4, now gives $x\in U$.

For (2), birationality gives isomorphisms of generic local rings, hence algebraic extensions of the generic residue fields. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-generically-algebraic-dvr-fibre] at the codimension-one DVR point: its local ring is normal and its fibre finite. Clause (3) gives $x\in U$. This proves all four clauses; for empty $X$ they are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (2), using the finite fibre argument of 0AB7.
